caption:
Feel like you can't afford a break? A short one may cost less than you think.

Researchers call breaks of ten minutes or less micro-breaks. A review of experiments found people who took them felt more energetic and less tired afterwards. On the whole, their work didn't suffer. Breaks didn't clearly help after mentally demanding tasks, though longer breaks did more.

How to try it at your next pause between tasks:
1. Stop, and step away from the screen.
2. Do something unrelated. Stretch, get a drink, or look outside.
3. Give it a few minutes, up to ten. Then go back.

These were mostly short studies, and people rated how they felt. If breaks feel impossible where you work, that is worth raising.

Save this for your next long stretch at the desk.

Research:
Albulescu, P., Macsinga, I., Rusu, A., Sulea, C., Bodnaru, A., & Tulbure, B. T. (2022). "Give me a break!" A systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy of micro-breaks for increasing well-being and performance. PLoS ONE, 17(8), e0272460. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0272460
